narrative: Material PL3__MBAA96BA shows stable high-volume demand (~50,514 units/day, CV=0.106) over 228 working days from March 2025 to March 2026, with a mild downward trend. Lead times are variable (CV=0.63), dominated by transport variance, necessitating a substantial safety stock of 81,937 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The storage capacity of 349,999 units hard-caps the order quantity at 268,061 units (down from the unconstrained EOQ of 662,912), but still delivers a 61.4% annual cost reduction versus the current SAP baseline.
warnings: Variable lead time detected (CV=0.63); monitor transport logistics
Storage capacity binds: EOQ reduced from 662,912 to 268,061 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: Stable, high-volume daily demand with variable lead times is best managed by a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The fixed reorder point triggers replenishment exactly when inventory falls to coverage of expected lead-time demand plus safety stock, minimising both stockout risk and unnecessary review overhead. The large MOQ and storage constraint make periodic-review policies less efficient here.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds hard at 349,999 units, reducing order quantity from the true EOQ of 662,912 to 268,061 units. This increases ordering frequency and annual ordering cost above the unconstrained optimum. If storage capacity can be expanded, significant additional savings are achievable.
